title: Faster start-up, a start-up screen, Remote access page, better Network page
notes: Faster: after a restart our Home screen is ready about 20 seconds sooner (about 60 seconds after power-on instead of 79). The less urgent clean-up now happens right after Home is up.

New: a plain dark "starting up" screen covers LG's own Home while the TV starts, so LG's promotions are not what you see first. It only appears if the TV would otherwise start on LG's Home: if it starts on an HDMI input or an app, nothing changes. There is a switch in Settings > Services & privacy (Show our own start-up screen), and you can put a picture called cover.png in the launcher folder to use your own.

New: Settings > Remote access shows how to find and reach the TV: its name, wired and Wi-Fi IP address, MAC address, the exact ssh and telnet commands, whether an SSH key is installed, and a Telnet on/off switch. SSH always stays on because it is the way back in; Telnet can only be switched off when an SSH key is installed.
Better: Settings > Network now also shows the router address, whether the Wi-Fi radio is on and which Wi-Fi networks the TV remembers. To join a new Wi-Fi network it still opens LG's own Settings.
Small: the swap memory is read back more efficiently (read-ahead off), and the invisible-pointer pictures are kept ready on flash so they cost no start-up time and no memory.

title: Memory guard: the TV protects itself when memory runs short
notes: New: a memory guard watches free memory and swapping every 10 seconds. If the TV starts to run short it first closes apps you are not using, then (if it gets serious) drops the Home photos and clears file cache, and puts everything back when things are calm. It is built for TVs with less memory too: it works in percentages and is stricter on a weaker TV.

New: Settings > About & updates now has a Memory guard section: its state, the lowest free memory and most swap since the TV started, how many times it had to step in, and a Memory profile choice (Automatic, Roomy, Standard, Weak). Weak keeps Home and the screensaver free of photos.
The guard has a switch in Settings > Services & privacy (Watch memory and protect the TV).

title: Settings opens almost instantly from Home, and LG's leftover menus are closed
notes: Faster: pressing the Settings button while you are on the Home screen now opens Settings in about a fifth of a second (it used to take a full second). From inside an app or an HDMI input it opens as quickly as before.

New: a few LG screens could still pop up from the remote: the microphone button (voice assistant), pressing Mute three times (LG's hidden service menu) and the Input Hub button. They are now closed the moment they open. There is a switch for it in Settings > Services & privacy (Close LG's leftover menus). This was tested by opening those screens directly, not yet with the real remote buttons.
LG's own Settings is still there under Settings > LG Settings (legacy), for Wi-Fi setup, accounts and channel tuning.

title: Software updates, and Settings keys that survive a restart
notes: New: Settings > Software updates. The TV can look at GitHub for a newer version of this project, show what changed, and install it with a safety copy (it goes back by itself if the new version does not start).

Fixed: after a restart the Settings, Input and Guide keys could turn back into LG's stock ones and the old LG Home could show up first. The start-up step waited for a Home screen that does not exist yet at that moment.
Home shows a small note at the top when an update is ready.
Fixed: LG's ad service could run for a few minutes after the Home screen restarted. It is now switched off again the moment Home is back.
